question: Can instance-level evidence selection improve visible cross-context correspondence within a fixed inspection batch?
hypothesis: Selecting the pair with strongest agreement across foreground, box and semantic crop views improves visible correspondence over first-encounter selection, and must be compared with foreground-nearest selection.
design: Adaptive descriptive mechanism experiment, motivated by the already inspected first-encounter pairs. No independent generalization claim. Freeze all first 50 discovery photos, all 25 cross-community families and existing embeddings. No filtering of families, no learned scorer, no semantic labels used in selection.
pair_eligibility: Two regions from the same r2 family, different canonical parents, different exact SHA256, different frozen global communities, both photos in the frozen first-50 discovery batch.

methods.first_encounter: Previously frozen pair: first encountered photo in each of two communities, higher family affinity within a tied photo.
methods.foreground_nearest: Maximum DINOv3 foreground cosine among eligible pairs; lexicographic region-ID tie break.
methods.view_consensus: Maximize minimum within-family eligible-pair percentile rank across DINOv3 foreground, DINOv3 box and SigLIP2 crop cosines; then maximize mean rank; then foreground cosine; then region IDs. Average ranks for ties. No thresholds.

primary_metric: Supported visible-pattern pairs out of all 25 families, with ambiguous and rejected counts retained. Same pair receives same adjudication across methods.
secondary: Paired wins and losses against both comparators
source redundancy or generic appearance recorded separately
review: Inspect every unique selected pair as full photos plus exact mask crops. Hide method and scores on review sheets; reviewer has seen baseline and is not independent or fully blinded. Broad visual correspondence does not establish component identity or novelty.
compute: Light CPU, only selected batch feature rows; existing memory-mapped arrays; no inference, extraction, cloud cost or GPU.
